newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK DEBT TO GDP RATIO SEEN FALLING IN 96 - BUDGET.
newsitem.headline: GREEK DEBT TO GDP RATIO SEEN FALLING IN 96 - BUDGET.

text.p: Greece's debt to GDP ratio is seen falling to 110.7 percent in 1996 from 111.8 percent in 1995, the 1997 budget, released on Friday, shows.
Greece has the third highest debt to GDP ratio in the EU after Belgium and Italy.
Interest payments on general government debt also eased to 12.4 percent of GDP in 1996 from 12.9 percent in 1995.
The 1997 budget was submitted to parliament by National Economy Minister Yannos Papandoniou. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
